Bell Pottinger 2

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The fall and fall of London PR firm, Bell Pottinger

Unique Selling Point:
An interview with Lord Tim Bell, founder of Bell Pottinger.

Summary:
Since the Gupta family hired Bell Pottinger to manage the family's public image over allegations of state capture, reports have circulated about their manipulation of the media and political narrative in South Africa. They denied all these allegations until the #GuptaLeaks showed emails between Duduzane Zuma and account manager Victoria Geoghegan that seemed to confirm the rumours.

Further information:
CEO James Henderson issued an apology in July 2017 admitting that the firm's conduct had been questionable, and that the people responsible had been fired. The DA then laid a formal complaint with the UK's Public Relations Association. They have upheld the complaint and James Henderson has resigned as CEO.

Press Release:


Bell Pottinger: The PR Disaster
The embattled British Public Relations Firm, Bell Pottinger faced yet another week of turmoil. CEO James
Henderson resigned ahead of the release of the scathing Henderson Report, which detailed how the
company, helped manufacture racial tension in South Africa. Now the British Public Relations and
Communications Association has banned the firm for the next five years. Ironically, could this public
relations disaster spell the end of this global PR giant? Carte Blanche untangles the web.

Script:


BELL POTTINGER 2

V/O: In January 2016, the Guptas hired controversial British PR firm Bell Pottinger to create a divisive propaganda campaign, that attacked so-called white monopoly capital. Targeting wealthy white individuals and corporates through offensive political speeches, blogs and social media, they stoked racial tension in South Africa, causing irreparable harm and contributing to our economic downgrade.

Ferial: What they did do was mastermind the big narrative of the campaign to divert attention from the looting we see happening, and to pin it on White Monopoly Capital and to harm various institutions or people.

V/O: Ferial Haffajee is the Editor of African Network of Centres for Investigative Reporting, who analysed the Gupta fake news empire.

Ferial: So, it spans the mass media, I’d argue the New Age and ANN7 to a number of websites, and then the really pernicious part of it was the activation of trolling twitter armies that for a while really sowed disinformation in our country.

V/O: Last week saw the dramatic downfall of this PR giant, when they were expelled from the UK’s Public Relations and Communications Association.

Francis: “Bell Pottinger’s membership is terminated with immediate effect. Bell Pottinger will not be eligible to re-apply for corporate membership of the PRCA for a minimum period of 5 years.”

V/O: This followed a complaint made by the Democratic Alliance, and presented by MP Phumzile van Damme

Phumzile: It's a bitter-sweet victory. I mean it's a victory on behalf of the people of South Africa who united and said to Bell Pottinger “not on our doorstep”. It's bitter because the people who hired Bell Pottinger, Duduzane Zuma and the Guptas are slithering away.

Link: There are seemingly endless revelations about state capture emerging from the so-called Gupta emails and other sources, but while our own law enforcement agencies appear either unwilling or unable to act, it's taken an independent regulator in another country to show us how it should be done.

V/O; We went to London to meet with the Director General of the PRCA, Francis Ingham, who explained some of the pressure they’ve been under.
03:10
Francis: I had people at my home at 4 o’clock in the morning, at 3 o’clock in the morning. I’ve had people asking how I would like to be killed? How I would like my children to be killed because there was an expectation we were going to do a cover-up. That was never what was going to happen.

John: Is the action taken against Bell Pottinger unprecedented?

Francis: These are very tough sanctions, and those sanctions befit the gravity of the malpractice that Bell Pottinger were involved in, and the gravity of the damage inflicted upon South Africa. And as an Englishman let me say that I am very sorry for what Bell Pottinger did in your country.

V/O: So how did it happen? We asked the founder and former Chairman of Bell Pottinger, Lord Tim Bell.

Tim: We went to Johannesburg and we went to see, we went to the compound, to the giant houses they have and we sat and listened to Gupta telling us how wonderful he was. They did talk a lot about how they made so much money and they had more money than they could spend. Then he said let's go to Cape Town. So, we got on a private plane and went down to Cape Town.

V/O: In the Bell Pottinger team was Jonathan Lehrle, Nick Lambert and lead partner Victoria Geoghegan. The Guptas were clear about what they wanted.

Tim: We want you to communicate that there's not enough black empowerment in terms of economic empowerment. They may have got the vote but they haven't got economic power.

V/O: Based on this premise they developed the white monopoly capital narrative. One of their targets was Johann Rupert, the Chairman of Richemont – an existing Bell Pottinger client.


Tim: I mentioned in the course of the conversation maybe I can talk to Johan Rupert and he might influence on some people. And they said don't talk to him he's a terrible person. I was slightly thrown by that because I've worked for Johann, I know Johann very well. And I knew that he was a considerable influence in these things. And they didn't seem to like him. I found that a conflict of interest.

John: And you made those feelings known to your colleagues?

Tim: I made it clear to James Henderson that I thought it was a conflict of interest.

John: But they forged ahead anyway?

Tim: Yes, they did. That’s why I left.

V/O: James Henderson was the CEO of Bell Pottinger. He is engaged to Heather Kerzner, the ex-wife of hotel magnate Sol Kerzner. Earlier this year she bought a 15% stake in Bell Pottinger. Together they own 37%.

Link: Lord Bell resigned from Bell Pottinger in August last year after suffering a stroke the previous April. But given his intimate role in signing up the Guptas – and despite his denials – questions still linger about the part he played in shaping the campaign.

Tim: I had nothing to do with the campaign. I didn't write the campaign strategy, I didn't write the plan, I didn't put the submission in. I went to a meeting. I was asked to do something. I said I'll oversee, making sure that was done. It was done and that was it.

John: There’s an email that Victoria Geoghegan wrote to Duduzane Zuma where she says that “Lord Bell will be available for strategic council as and when required.”

Tim: It's a perfectly normal thing to do. I'm the head of the company. I'm available to everybody.

V/O: In fact, Lord Bell claims he was deliberately side-lined by Henderson.

Tim: James Henderson worked very closely with Victoria Geoghegan; they talked to each other all the time, they had secret meetings and secret discussions. They eliminated me from those conversations, they didn't want me involved. And that's the truth. My role in the company was rapidly diminishing. I was rapidly not being consulted about things, not told about what was going on. I wasn't there, I wasn't there. Most of the time I was away sick anyway.

Link: James Henderson has maintained throughout this saga that he was kept in the dark about the detail of the Gupta campaign. But that is disputed by Lord Tim Bell who says Henderson is a micro-manager who would have insisted on keeping tabs on Victoria Geoghegan and her team.

Tim: He had hired her and he promoted her and he made a great fuss of her. She tried to befriend me, and she used to have me on her screensaver on her computer. But she wasn't sincere. She’s a very ambitious girl.

V/O: In July Victoria Geoghegan was fired, and Henderson issued an apology for the inappropriate and offensive campaign. Even though it generated over 45 000 documents, he claimed that senior management had been misled by the team in South Africa.

John: James Henderson claims to have been kept in the dark throughout this entire process. Should we believe him?

Tim: Well, he's lying, he’s lying. He wasn't kept in the dark. He knew exactly what was going on.

John: Where is Victoria Geoghegan now?

Tim: She's suing them for wrongful dismissal...

John: If she's suing them for wrongful dismissal it does suggest that she doesn't believe she's done anything wrong.

Tim: She doesn't believe she did, no.

John: Do you think she did?

Tim: I'm sure she did.

Link: Bell Pottinger has denied that its South Africa campaign, concocted in the non-descript building in the background, knowingly fuelled racial tensions, but Carte Blanche has seen email correspondence which appears to contradict that.

V/O: In March 2016, Victoria updated senior management, including Lord Bell and James Henderson, about extending the Gupta. She added “As we have known from the start, we are in the middle of a civil war with the Guptas and allies on one side, and Johann Rupert and others on the other side. More mud will inevitably be thrown. However, it is difficult to turn down such a large retainer with the potential for more.”

Phumzile: They saw a big cheque and threw their ethics out the window and did what they wanted to do in order to earn this money.

Tim: It was one of the largest clients. Not the largest, but one of the largest. He thought that he would take more money from them than he would lose from other clients.

John: So, there was a bit of risk involved?

Tim: He didn’t think Investec would fire us; he didn’t think Richemont would fire us, he didn’t think Mediclinic would fire us, but they did. We got messages from South African clients saying you’re associated with the Guptas, you’re not worth dealing with. James ignored all that. He thought it was less money than the money he would get from the Guptas.

V/O: We wanted to meet with Bell Pottinger, but they are not giving interviews.

Link The fallout from the PRCA ruling has been dramatic. In the past week, the Bell Pottinger empire has crumbled like a house of cards. It’s reputation in tatters, the once mighty Bell Pottinger is now up for sale.

Tim: Look it took me 30 years to build that business into a premier brand, the greatest brand in the marketplace. It’s taken them one year to destroy it.

Francis: If you are in the business of improving and managing people’s reputations and your own reputation collapses within the course of three months, then you’re probably not very good at your job.

V/O: There have been calls for Bell Pottinger to pay back the 1.2 million Pounds.

Ferial: And if you trace the genesis of that money, it was all taxpayers’ money. It has been coming out pretty clearly, it belongs to the South African citizen and the taxpayer.

John: Do you regret ever laying eyes on the Guptas?

Tim: Yes, of course I do. I'm very sorry I met the Guptas. They were terrible people. And they asked us to do things that weren't a good thing to do. It's resulted in Henderson losing his job, the company going down the tubes, in 200 people losing their jobs, who were completely innocent. Do I regret it? Yes.

V/O: During his recent live interview on BBC Newsnight, Tim Bell’s cellphone kept ringing. Apparently, the caller was none other than Johann Rupert.

Tim: I’m very touched about what Johann Rupert said to me. He said thank you for being honourable. That’s true, I was honourable.
